analysis: Only GitHub Actions CI workflows changed; no provider, coordinator, crypto, attestation or cache-storage source changed, so the T-041/TB-007/TB-011 controls are untouched. Checked: (1) Concurrency blocks with cancel-in-progress in desktop, docs-impact, landing and nightly-linear-package. The group is keyed on PR number or ref. This only supersedes stale runs and does not weaken permissions (contents: read stays). A push to master can cancel an earlier master run of the same workflow, which is a CI availability and coverage tradeoff, not a security issue. (2) provider-plan.yml adds a run_tests input and a cluster_gpu output. The label and event values reach the shell only through env vars (GPU_LABELED, EVENT_NAME, REF), so there is no script injection. GPU shards are now limited to workflow_dispatch, master/main push or the run-gpu-ci label. The build-cluster and build-provider lanes no longer run when the tree was already tested on a push (lines 202-203 of head). I could not see consumers of those lanes, so any downstream dependence on them is unverified. This is a CI coverage change, not a threat-model control. (3) provider-release-cache.yml replaces the master push trigger with a daily schedule behind a fail-open gate job (actions: read, github.token). The gate skips the warm when no relevant path changed since the last green run. The path list drops scripts/**, so script-only changes no longer trigger an immediate warm. The release cache can therefore be staler. This is a performance concern only, since release builds are still produced by release-swift.yml. The warm job still uses blacksmith for master and schedule runs and the plane only for PRs, so privilege and trust placement is unchanged. Gate parsing reads only GitHub API JSON and passes it to python by file, with no untrusted interpolation. Remaining question for integration: whether release-swift.yml or other workflows rely on the removed push-time build lanes or cache warms. This is not visible in the supplied evidence.
